newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss keep envoy to Iran in Berne for consultation.
newsitem.headline: Swiss keep envoy to Iran in Berne for consultation.

text.p: Switzerland will keep its ambassador to Iran in Berne while it decides how to respond to a German court ruling that Tehran ordered the 1992 murders of four Kurdish activists, Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti said on Friday.
"We do not have to recall our ambassador from Tehran because he happens to already be in Berne," Cotti told Swiss television in an interview released ahead of transmission on Friday night.
"We will keep him in Berne with the same aim as the European Union, namely for consultations, for determining our own policy."

Cotti described the ruling as "a courageous verdict of an independent German court" that raised concerns for Switzerland, but added he did not want to give a final response until he had a chance to read it in its entirety.
"But I find the verdict is especially worrying if it in fact is true that high Iranian officials are involved," he said.

Germany and Sweden recalled their ambassadors from Iran after the ruling on Thursday and the EU invited other members to join the action. Australia has also ordered its envoy home and Britain said it would do so shortly.
Neutral Switzerland has represented U.S. diplomatic interests in Iran since the U.S. embassy in Tehran was seized by Iranian students in 1980.
